_RULE_BEFORE_YOU_EDIT: This file is a COPY. Cinemail keeps its own, and the two must stay identical.
Do not change any number here without asking the Cinemail session first, and
do not accept a change from it without checking the number yourself against a
file rather than against a claim.
That rule is not ceremony. Every wrong number in this file's history came from
one side measuring the wrong thing and the other side believing it:
- 1.189 was reported as the envelope aspect three times. It is Cinemail's
INK box, which includes the reel and the film strip. The envelope is 1.44.
Found by measuring their isolated envelope layer instead of the composite;
confirmed independently at 1.438 on their side against 1.441 on ours.
- A flap apex at 42.7% across, and a flap edge angle of 38.2 degrees, were
both withdrawn as antialiasing noise on a nearly flat edge.
Measure the isolated thing, not the composite. Say which file you measured.
_howThisWasEstablished: Not decided - discovered. Cinemail's envelope and Tunemail's draft were
generated separately, months apart, from prompts describing the same thing.
Measured against each other they turn out to already agree:
There was an apparent disagreement of 1.443 against 1.189 for a while. That
was an error of mine: 1.189 is Cinemail's INK box, which includes the reel
and the film strip, not its envelope. Comparing an ink box with a paper box.
Two other numbers were retracted along the way and are recorded so nobody
reintroduces them: a flap apex at 42.7% across (noise - their flap edge is
so flat near the apex that the topmost pixel is decided by antialiasing) and
a flap edge angle of 38.2 degrees (from the same bad basis; at this aspect
it puts the apex below the envelope floor).

envelope._aspect: width / height of the paper box. Cinemail 1193x827 at 2048; the Tunemail draft 1193x827 as well.
envelope._backWall: The top corner of the back wall, as fractions of the envelope box. Mirrored on the right.
envelope._flap: The front flap's top edge is a straight line from the side to the apex. Measured slope 1.049 of the height per unit of width, linear across x=0.15 to x=0.50, so a straight segment is faithful rather than an approximation.
envelope._apexCentred: Cinemail's looked off-centre at 42.7%; re-measurement showed that was antialiasing on a nearly flat edge. Nothing argues against centred, and Dafa's instinct was to centre it.

outline._colour: Cinemail's fill census: 27 of 37 paths are #0D0D1A, which is also its background. The mark reads as cut out of the field rather than drawn on it. Identical between siblings for free as long as the field is.
outline._stroke: 63 samples across Cinemail's envelope left edge, median run 24px at 2048.

perApp._: What each sibling is allowed to differ in.
varies: the object rising out of the envelope

_knownLimit: Cinemail's envelope, as it exists in docs/icon-layers/2-envelope.svg, is a fragment: the film strip covers its right shoulder entirely and a notch is cut where the reel sits in front. There is no complete authored envelope anywhere in that repo. The numbers above come from its uncontaminated left half, mirrored - which is why the apex being centred matters more than it looks.
